clue.text: Reject instruction to set sail

definitions.meaning: a discarded thing or person, something thrown aside
the order to untie a boat's mooring ropes and get under way

explanation.surface: A rejected sailor's orders to put out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a discarded item is thrown off, and loosing a vessel's ropes is the cry heard as it leaves port.

clue.text: Match a red trim

parts.note: Com is an abbreviation for communist, a red
to pare is to cut away the edges

explanation.surface: A red ribbon matched to a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken or set side by side, as one measures items against each other.

clue.text: Totally ignored on being elevated to a West Midlands see

definitions.meaning: shunned, given the silent treatment

definitions.text: on being elevated to a West Midlands see
definitions.meaning: posted as bishop to the cathedral city near Birmingham

explanation.surface: A cleric ignored by everyone after promotion to a bishopric in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means shunned; read literally it describes a cleric dispatched to the diocese of Coventry, a city in the West Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: an idiom for being ostracised, and a literal posting to the Coventry diocese.

clue.text: Love to take advantage of the river

parts.note: O is zero, love in tennis
use, exploit

explanation.surface: A lover makes the most of a riverside day.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring 'love' is nil, shown as O.
explanation.definitionFit: A river in Yorkshire, one of several English rivers of the name.

clue.text: Jump up in fury in a cheap cinema

indicators.note: in tells us the jumping word sits inside the fury word

parts.note: a fit, an outburst of rage
leap, spring upwards

explanation.surface: Leaping up in anger at a shabby picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLEAPIT is British slang for a run-down cinema, supposedly flea-infested.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a shabby, run-down picture house thought to harbour vermin.

clue.text: Swear to hail the king

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting, a salute
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Taking an oath of loyalty while saluting the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm solemnly is a synonym for declaring on oath.

annotationWithheld.clue: Fruit delivered in a case prior to party

clue.text: Relaxation in Battersea's Edwardian homes

indicators.note: homes says the words before it house the letters wanted, running across the word gap

explanation.surface: Relaxing in the Edwardian houses of a South London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort and freedom from effort, rest.

clue.text: Priest enters vessel prepared to win

indicators.note: enters tells us the priest word goes inside the vessel word

parts.note: a pail, a bucket
Rev, short for Reverend

explanation.surface: A clergyman steps aboard a ship ready for victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared to' is padding before the definition 'win'; 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph, come out on top.

clue.text: Army officer on manoeuvre requiring surgical precision

definitions.note: the definition describes a big surgical procedure, given loosely as a descriptive phrase

parts.note: a major, rank above captain
a military operation, an exercise

explanation.surface: An army officer on exercise needs pinpoint accuracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious surgical procedure, or figuratively any big undertaking.

clue.text: Unusually fit man set to rise high in government

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the following words appear in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A fit man is poised for a remarkable climb up the political ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior cabinet-level post in the UK, a senior rank within a department of state.

clue.text: Takes steps to get legislation passed

definitions.meaning: does something, takes action
laws passed by a parliament, statutes

explanation.surface: Measures are taken to push a new law through.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: performs deeds, and statutes enacted by parliament.

clue.text: He would only eat lean fish

definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme man who could eat no fat
a small sea fish of the herring family

explanation.surface: A fussy diner who would only eat lean fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme 'could eat no fat'; the same surname is a small fish, so the clue reads as one fussy eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the rhyme's fat-shunning husband shares his name with a small herring-like fish.

clue.text: I have to come back a little bit

indicators.note: coming back means the short word before it is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: I have to return a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest Greek letter is used for a very small quantity, a jot.

clue.text: He swindles the staff

definitions.meaning: a cheat, a fraudster
a shepherd's or bishop's hooked stick

explanation.surface: A con man swindles the workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a criminal, and a hooked shepherd's stick.

clue.text: Fork produced by early Englishman

definitions.meaning: the corner where two lines diverge
a member of the Germanic tribe that settled England

explanation.surface: Cutlery made by an early English settler.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the spread between two branching lines, and one of the Germanic settlers who gave England its name.

clue.text: But include the right passage

indicators.note: include tells us the word for 'but' takes the next piece within it

parts.note: except, meaning apart from
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An objection, yet one that admits the correct section of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract, a short section quoted from a longer text.

clue.text: To admit objective is to one's disadvantage

definitions.note: the definition describes a self-inflicted setback, a noun phrase given loosely as a verb phrase

parts.note: to own is to confess or acknowledge
an aim or target

explanation.surface: Confessing one's real aim may backfire.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, putting the ball in your own net; figuratively any act that harms oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring into one's own net is the stock image of a self-inflicted blow.

clue.text: Various versions call him Lord

indicators.note: versions suggests the letters of the word before it are rendered in a different form

explanation.surface: Various translations of scripture call him Lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian title for Christ as redeemer of mankind.

clue.text: Put one's foot down and made an impression

definitions.meaning: brought a foot down hard
printed or embossed a mark

explanation.surface: Someone who asserted authority and left a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: struck the ground with a foot, and marked with a die or rubber stamp.

clue.text: Back to Southern Europe with more fire-power

parts.note: the rear, the back part
the Med, the Mediterranean region

explanation.surface: Returning to the Mediterranean with heavier guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplied again with weapons, so better armed.

clue.text: Able to pay for paint-stripper, maybe

definitions.meaning: having enough money to meet debts
a liquid that dissolves things, paint-stripper being one example

explanation.surface: Someone who can afford the paint-stripper.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: financially sound, and a dissolving liquid such as turpentine.

clue.text: Instruction class for newly drafted marines

indicators.note: newly drafted suggests the letters are written out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A training session for recruits just joining the marines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial or discussion group for teaching students.

clue.text: Set one's sights on getting coached

definitions.meaning: aimed, as with a gun
taught, prepared by practice

explanation.surface: An athlete aiming high while being coached.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: pointed a weapon at, and taught through practice.

clue.text: Complaint from airman heading north-east

parts.note: AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
NE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pilot flying north-east has a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition, complaint in the sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Majorcan resort for parents about fifty

indicators.note: about tells us the parents word goes around the next piece

parts.note: pa and ma, father and mother
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean holiday spot for a couple nearing fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Majorca, a popular Balearic holiday city.

clue.text: Thanks to commercial backing, the facts are revealed

indicators.note: backing says the word for commercial is read from right to left

parts.note: ad, a television or newspaper advertisement
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: With an advertiser's support, the truth comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Information, a set of recorded figures or particulars.

clue.text: Italian greeting conveyed to American intelligence by cipher

parts.note: the CIA, the US spy agency
a cipher is a zero, the figure O

explanation.surface: A coded hello passed to US spies.
explanation.definitionFit: The casual Italian hello or goodbye.

clue.text: A little lower than the knee

definitions.text: A little lower than the knee

parts.words: A little lower than the knee
parts.note: read as a small mooing animal, a young lower, rather than a point just below the knee

explanation.surface: Describing a body part just below the knee.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lower' is something that moos, a cow; a little one is its young. The surface points to the back of the leg, which shares the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a young bovine and the fleshy back of the lower leg.

clue.text: A cavalier opponent

parts.note: read as one who fought against the Cavaliers, the royalists of the English Civil War, rather than a casual opponent

explanation.surface: A carefree, offhand adversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' looks like an adjective meaning offhand; here it is a royalist of the English Civil War, and their enemies were the supporters of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roundhead, a supporter of the Commons side against King Charles I.

clue.text: Common gangster disguise

definitions.meaning: a hoodlum, a low-level criminal
a covering for the head and face

explanation.surface: An ordinary mobster wears a mask.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: slang short for hoodlum, and a cowl pulled over the head to hide the face.

clue.text: Again paid the penalty for being genteel

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
fined, made to pay money as a punishment

explanation.surface: Someone who paid up a second time for putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished and well-mannered, cultivated in taste.
